decisions.evidence: The variants differ only by the audible contraction it'll/it will; grammar cannot identify the recording's wording.
Bunko is the plausible party-game term and the colon fits the headline, while Funko does not fit the described game; no repository authority confirms the proper spelling.
Runnin' versus running represents an audible elision and cannot be selected from grammar or hash count.
The filename explicitly identifies Chrono, and revision 1 uses that exact authoritative character spelling.
The killed_by_lash filename directly identifies Lash; Flash is a generated name error.
I got a heal and I gotta heal are both plausible but semantically different spoken phrases.
Eldritch fits the occult setting and company context better than Eldridge, but the repository has no independent authoritative spelling.
You will/You'll is an audible contraction. The separate official Hidden King revision is later patron material and must not be used to collapse these prototype recordings.

Revision 2 is the coherent response to the preceding symposium request; revision 1's Do I imagine is malformed, while revision 0 has plausible fillers and different tense that require audio to exclude.
Failed to protect is the coherent family-duty statement; sailed to protect is a generated homophone error.
Buyin' versus buying is an audible elision; the unrelated revision 0 remains outside this component.
Both Urdkeeper and Urthkeeper are plausible attempts at an Oathkeeper-story proper name, with no authoritative repository occurrence resolving it.
Let the Guardian deal with that one is grammatical and is mirrored at the ghost alias path; Let's the Guardian is malformed.
The generated revisions vary an audible contraction and word order; the official madman line is wholly different and remains separate.
If you ask me is the conventional complete introductory clause; You ask me can be colloquial speech, so audio is needed for high confidence. The official line is unrelated.
The filename establishes Kelvin later in the line, but the initial Kevin may be an intentional mistaken-name joke rather than a transcription error.
The variants differ by the audible opening interjection Oh, which grammar cannot supply or remove.
Ursyse and Urassi are competing unverified proper-name spellings in the Oathkeeper story; no independent repository evidence resolves them.
Breach, wreath, and wrath are all generated interpretations of the same response, and the Wraith-lift filename does not establish the spoken noun.
Aether Son is the only candidate shaped like an occult title and fits a statement about Ghost's powers, but it lacks independent authoritative spelling evidence.
They're/They are is an audible contraction and both forms are grammatical.
Revision 1 is the only coherent complete sentence: Vindicta was a powerless child when condemned; cowardice/cowards cannot grammatically occupy that predicate position.
Our purple walker is under attack is grammatical and refers to the single color-lane Walker; revision 0 lacks the required possessive or verb.
Power and powers are both grammatical and differ in audible number.
Come at the queen is the clear challenge; Comet the queen is a generated segmentation error.
The filename refers to the single boss Guardian, and parallel fencer, Viscous, and Gigawatt lines use The Guardian will deal with them.
The parallel nano_ap_reminder alias has the exact complete sentence I can't forget to upgrade my palace.
Never should have and I never should have are both grammatical spoken variants; the corrupt revision 0 is outside the fuzzy component.
The final-name Ivy alias independently carries I wonder what the Arroyos are up to, supporting revision 1 while preserving the Tengu/Ivy era alias distinction.
Fop is a meaningful old-fashioned insult fitting Warden's diction; flop is also grammatically possible and no parallel line confirms the noun.
An answer and any answer are both grammatical and semantically distinct audible wording.
A seat at the table with skeptics refers to people and is coherent; with skepticism cannot denote the people controlling the table.
The killed character is Kelvin, making parka an explicit cold-weather pun; park is incoherent in context.
All right is the standard two-word spelling required by the transcription guidelines; the two variants represent the same spoken phrase.
Who is/Who's is an audible contraction and both forms are grammatical.
Target and targets differ in audible number and both are plausible for Haze.
The check-items filename and authoritative Holliday spelling support Check out what Holliday bought; boughts is ungrammatical.
Them versus 'em records an audible elision and cannot be chosen by grammar.
The check_items filename establishes bought; brought is a generated lexical error. Holliday is the authoritative final name for the Astro-era target.
Parallel Lash check-item lines use the characteristic Ooh opening, including the Ivy/Tengu counterpart; revision 0 matches that pattern.
Check out what Vindicta bought is grammatical and matches the check_items filename; revision 0's what's plus bought is malformed.
I am/I'm is an audible contraction and both readings are grammatical.
Hm and Hmm are both conventional spellings of the same non-lexical vocalization, with no repository rule selecting one.
The filename requires McGinnis, while both component revisions transcribe guiness/guinness; neither existing component revision is correct.
The component's Great talent bots/bot readings are corrupt and do not name the filename target Orion; even the outside Great Talon revision conflicts with authoritative Grey Talon naming.
You are lost, Ivy is the grammatical direct address and agrees lexically with the official line. The official Archmother wording remains separate later patron material.
Ah versus Ah-ah is an audible vocalization difference and cannot be inferred from grammar.
'em versus them is an audible elision and both forms fit the sentence.
Revision 1 contains an additional audible I just repetition; narrative context cannot establish whether it was spoken.
Bleak Carnival is a plausible ominous proper name in this setting, whereas Bleet appears to be a generated near-homophone; no independent repository authority confirms it.
Takin' versus taking represents an audible elision, and the hashes are evenly split.
The filename identifies Grey Talon, but both revisions say Great talent(s); neither existing component revision is correct.
The filename identifies Grey Talon, but both revisions say Great talent(s); neither existing component revision is correct.
Orion is the prototype-era alias for the target later named Grey Talon, but both revisions say Great talent(s); neither is an authoritative name transcription.
The final-name Dynamo alias independently has The students are not gonna believe me when I talk about my day, confirming revision 0.
The filename target is Viscous, while both revisions say Biscuit; bought versus has bought cannot repair the missing authoritative name.
He/she tracks the Astro-to-Holliday prototype/final character evolution and can represent genuinely separate era-specific recordings; the final ghost alias uses she.
Weak forms the intended contrast with strong; week is a generated homophone that makes the maxim incoherent.
The filename identifies Grey Talon, while both revisions say Great ammo; neither existing component revision is correct.
The filename identifies Grey Talon, while both revisions say Great talent/talent's; neither existing component revision is correct.
